pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as step one — kettlebell efficiency, three to four sessions of 30-40 minutes, plus five-to-ten-minute daily mobility protocols usable at his desk, framed against his packed schedule. The prospect tied it to his own cultural frame unprompted when the rep cited the cross-legged sit-to-stand longevity test: 'Yeah, that's one of the tests we do use actually, in our culture.' On the approach itself: 'Oh, definitely... that's exactly what I'm looking for. It's like, you know, you tell me what to do. And I think I need to work enough to develop that muscle memory.'

Delivered as three variables — what you eat, when you eat, how much you eat — with an eating window and a permitted weekly indulgence. Prospect agreed by mapping it onto behaviour he already has rather than by engaging with anything new: 'Oh, definitely. mean, that's exactly what I do, actually. We try not to eat, you know, no snacking. We don't have any sodas.' Note the rep handled the vegetarian constraint by pivoting to the prospect's eggs and occasional chicken — 'He's eating a lot of red meat, but we have also vegetarians in our program. But you said you eat chicken and you eat eggs and that's good' — rather than describing how a mostly plant-based protein target would be programmed.

Presented as the game changer for this specific prospect and the strongest fit to his stated gap — one-to-one design with Trevor, video form checks, weekly check-ins, Trevor's personal cell number, over-communication encouraged. The prospect's response was positive but conditional and raised a mechanic the rep had not anticipated: 'if I'm working directly with him, that's great. The only question I have is, like, since I have to send videos and, you know, it's kind of personal, so as long as the platform is secure and that thing is taken care of, then I don't have any other questions.'

anchors.raw: I have actually seen a lot of programs on like through Facebook, whether it's Ladder, Better Me, Men's Health, and all those kinds of things. But this one was like kettlebell specific.
anchors.note: He arrived having comparison-shopped a set of consumer fitness apps priced in tens of dollars a month. The rep never asked what any of them cost or what he had paid, so the gap between that reference frame and $6,000 was never measured or closed.

anchors.raw: $6,000 for six months. So $1,000 a month?
anchors.note: The prospect's first instinct on hearing the price was to divide it into a monthly rate, which is the app-subscription frame reasserting itself. The rep corrected it well — 'It's $6,000 for six months of the transformation... It's not like a gym membership, right?' — and the prospect accepted the reframe. One of the cleanest anchor rebuttals in the batch.

anchors.raw: each of the certifications that I'm looking forward to, there are easily 3K or 4K or more. So those are the things that we are, you know, looking forward to.
anchors.note: Cuts both ways and the rep exploited neither side. It undercuts because $6,000 is competing directly against two named alternative spends and a September trip. But it also demonstrates capacity — a man who routinely writes 3K-4K cheques for professional certifications can fund this, and the rep never made the comparison that he is willing to invest in his career at that level but not yet in the body that has to carry it.

anchors.raw: you never know, as we have known for the last two years, things can come up, and they can come up really like in a bad way. So I hope that's not the case anymore. I hope we are done, but you never know. So you always have to have some room for unexplained.
anchors.note: A reserve-holding anchor rather than a price one — he keeps liquidity uncommitted because of two years of unpleasant surprises. Any payment structure has to survive that instinct, and none was offered.

unmet_demand.want: Assurance that the platform he uploads personal shirtless training video to is secure
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep answered a different question — he addressed who would view the video ('You're working only with Trevor. There is no other coach over there') rather than how the platform handles or protects it. There is almost certainly a real answer available; nobody gave it.

unmet_demand.want: A nutrition plan built for a mostly plant-based Indian vegetarian household
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep acknowledged vegetarians exist in the programme, then immediately routed around the constraint by leaning on the prospect's occasional eggs and chicken. He never described how the protein target is met on a plant-based diet, which is the actual question for a vegetarian starting strength training.

unmet_demand.want: A way to start now that works around 3K-4K certifications and September travel
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Flexibility was mentioned in the abstract — 'we have various ways we can work around the finances' — but no instalment structure, deposit or start date was ever put on the table before the call ended. The company permits deposits; none was offered.

unmet_demand.want: Clarity on how long the offer and the slot remain available while he decides
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked directly — 'how long do I have if I have to get back to you on this before we actually start, commit, and move forward with this?' — and never received an answer. The rep responded by discussing his own calendar rather than the offer's terms.
